newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa details accelerated depreciation scheme.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa details accelerated depreciation scheme.

text.p: The South African Finance Ministry has detailed a proposed tax concession on depreciation of plant and buildings, cutting the write-off periods to three and 10 years respectively.
The concessions were first announced by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel in his June 14 macroeconomic strategy for growth, employment and redistribution.

A draft memorandum explaining the Revenue Laws Amendment Bill going before parliament on September 11 says the concession will apply to new or used machinery or plant acquired or brought into use between July 1 this year and September 30, 1999.

"The effect of the accelerated wear and tear allowance is that the present allowance of 20 percent per annum is increased to 33 1/3 percent per annum...determined on a straight-line basis," the memorandum says.
The cost of building or improving factory buildings will be written of at 10 percent a year instead of the current five percent a year.
The concession applies to work begun between July 1 this year and September 30, 1999, and brought into use by March 31, 2000.
